thesisQuality.note: Regulated grid demand is durable and rate-base investment is evidenced, but value capture remains regulator-dependent.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Guidance and multi-year growth outlook are intact, with financing substantially executed, offset by capital intensity.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: About 15.4x trailing earnings and 4.0% yield provide reasonable headroom versus supported mid-single-digit EPS growth, not exceptional asymmetry.

catalystScore.note: Rate-base build and large-load interconnections are identifiable catalysts but timing is regulator/project dependent.

governancePower.note: Current proxy/governance materials support ordinary public-company oversight; evidence does not justify exceptional stewardship scoring.

alignment2036.note: Transmission/distribution reliability and electrification are critical long-duration infrastructure needs.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Multiple regulated utilities and jurisdictions diversify demand while sharing grid-investment capability.

bottleneckControl.note: Exelon controls regulated delivery infrastructure in constrained service territories, though generation/transmission scarcity and regulation limit control.

scenarioRobustness.note: Regulated utility demand is resilient across scenarios, but rate and financing sensitivity remain.

substitutionResilience.note: Electric distribution/transmission networks have high replacement friction, tempered by regulatory and technology changes at the margin.

supplyChainResilience.note: Scale and multi-utility operations support resilience, but generation/transmission equipment constraints remain material.

pricingPower.note: Regulated recovery supports cost pass-through but is constrained by affordability and commission approval rather than unilateral pricing.

risk.note: Moderate risk from regulation, financing, equity issuance and uncertain conversion of large-load demand.

confidence.note: Current issuer, SEC governance and independent market/demand sources provide broad coverage; project-level economics remain unknown.

thesis: Regulated grid investment and electrification provide durable demand with moderate valuation support, while regulation and capital intensity cap upside quality.
keyRisk: Regulatory/financing pressure or speculative large-load demand delays rate-base conversion and per-share returns.
nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 earnings and updates to load, rate-base and financing execution.
